profile.name: Karan Gattani
profile.bio: Helping startups and enterprises transform business problems into scalable software solutions through structured analysis, workflow design, AI automation, and product strategy.
profile.approach: I work at the intersection of business and technology. My work involves understanding stakeholder problems, defining software requirements, creating business documentation, designing workflows, validating APIs, supporting Agile delivery, and ensuring that engineering teams build the right product. I specialize in AI Automation, CRM platforms, SaaS applications, and workflow optimization.

procureflow.background: ProcureFlow was commissioned by a mid-sized manufacturing client operating across 4 factories. They purchased raw metals, parts, and equipment from 120+ active vendors. All interactions, bid invitations, quotation receipts, comparison sheets, and final approvals were managed via email strings and complex local Excel files.
procureflow.problem: The manual approach had critical flaws: it took over 14 days to approve a simple raw material purchase, comparison sheets were often error-ridden, and audit logs did not exist. This led to factory downtime due to delays and suspicious vendor selections.
goals: Reduce purchase cycle time from 14 days to under 4 days.
Create an immutable digital audit log for all vendor quotes and selections.
Ensure data security and access controls for internal vs. external users.
challenges: Legacy Vendor Resistance: External vendors preferred using simple emails and were reluctant to learn complex portal systems.
Complex Approval Hierarchies: Approvals depended on department, budget size, and item category (e.g., machinery over $50k needed CFO approval).
requirements: Req 01: Vendors must be able to submit PDF quotes that are automatically parsed (OCR).
Req 02: System must generate a side-by-side comparison sheet comparing unit prices, delivery terms, and vendor rating scores.
Req 03: Workflows must route approval requests sequentially based on a configurable matrix rules engine.
Req 04: Audit logs must capture IP addresses, timestamps, and active user IDs for every bid state change.
procureflow.solution: We designed a SaaS procurement platform featuring a vendor portal and an internal staff dashboard. The vendor portal simplified bid entry, while the staff portal consolidated comparisons and automated routing. I designed a customized rule-based approval workflows engine that dynamically assigns approvers depending on transaction parameters.
procureflow.workflows: The vendor submits a quote → System extracts fields and alerts the buyer → Buyer checks comparisons and pushes to approval → System checks the value and routes to Manager (and VP if >$10k) → Once approved, PDF Purchase Order is autogenerated and emailed to the vendor.
procureflow.wireframes: Created low-fidelity Figma boards detailing: (1) Vendor bid submission form, (2) Procurement officer's quote comparison spreadsheet view, and (3) Factory manager's mobile quick-approval panel.
userStories: As a Procurement Manager, I want to view a comparative table of bids for a request so that I can select the optimal vendor.
As a Factory Manager, I want to approve a purchase order via mobile email links so that I don't delay materials delivery.
procureflow.acceptanceCriteria: Given a manager clicks on the 'Approve' link in their notification email, when the transaction is pending their authorization, then the system must transition the status to 'Approved', record the timestamp in the audit DB, and send a notification to the buyer.
procureflow.apiRequirements: POST /api/v1/purchases/approve\\nHeaders: Authorization: Bearer <token>\\nPayload: { 'purchase_order_id': 'PO-9921', 'action': 'APPROVE', 'comments': 'Urgent stock replenishment approved.' }\\nResponse: { 'status': 'success', 'po_status': 'APPROVED', 'timestamp': '2026-07-17T12:00:00Z' }
procureflow.uat: Conducted UAT with 4 factory supervisors and 2 directors. Tracked usability bugs on Jira. Reworked the mobile quick-action buttons based on supervisor feedback.
procureflow.outcome: ProcureFlow launched successfully. The average procurement delay dropped from 14.5 days to 3.2 days. The system logged 1,200 transactions in its first quarter, resulting in 100% auditable trail compliance.
procureflow.lessons: Keeping vendor entry fields extremely minimal was key. Overcomplicating the vendor onboarding form caused friction, so we simplified it to a drag-and-drop PDF upload with automated form pre-fill using AI OCR parser.

careflow.background: CareFlow's client, a home healthcare agency with 250+ nurses and therapists, scheduled patient visits manually. Coordinators matched patient schedules with caregiver availability and qualification rules on large office spreadsheets.
careflow.problem: Coordinators spent hours adjusting schedules when nurses called in sick. It took over 4 hours to re-assign visits, causing delayed client visits, transport inefficiency, and compliance violations due to mismatch of caregiver qualifications to patient needs.
goals: Cut scheduling time from hours to minutes.
Integrate GPS routing to minimize travel overhead.
challenges: HIPAA Privacy Regulations: Patient medical data must be encrypted and protected at all stages.
Complex Staff Availabilities: Caregivers work irregular part-time shifts and have varying geographic limits.
requirements: Req 01: Schedulers must see alerts when matching a nurse whose certifications do not meet the patient prescription requirements.
Req 02: Caregivers must receive scheduling updates on their mobile app in real-time.
Req 03: Caregiver travel paths must be optimized automatically using mapping APIs.
careflow.solution: A web CRM for coordinators combined with a mobile companion app for field nurses. The core match engine compares patient records to staff profile tables using criteria weightings (availability 40%, location distance 30%, skill fit 30%).
careflow.workflows: Patient booking logged → CareFlow engine queries active staff directories → Ranks top 5 matches → Coordinator selects recommendation → Notification sent to nurse's mobile app to accept/reject.
careflow.wireframes: Mocked scheduling dashboard with color-coded calendar blocks, qualifications tags, and route map overlays.
userStories: As a Coordinator, I want the system to filter nurses by specialty license so that I don't assign an unqualified nurse to a complex pediatric case.
As a Nurse, I want to toggle my status to 'Offline' in real-time so that coordinators don't assign me urgent visits outside shift hours.
careflow.acceptanceCriteria: Given a scheduler is booking a patient visit requiring 'Wound Care' expertise, when they attempt to assign a caregiver lacking the active certification, then the system must block the assignment and present a validation error.
careflow.uat: Ran UAT dry-runs with 3 schedulers and 10 field nurses. Verified offline data storage sync on the mobile app to handle weak internet zones.
careflow.outcome: Coordinator scheduling overhead was cut by 70%. Average nurse travel distances dropped by 1.8 miles per visit, reducing travel cost reimbursements significantly.
careflow.lessons: Handling edge cases like shift cancellations in real-time required a solid push-notification framework rather than periodic polling, which drained mobile device batteries.

insureai.background: The client was a regional insurance company handling property loss claims. The intake process for claim details (emails, phone call transcripts, damage photos) took days, creating client dissatisfaction.
insureai.problem: Staff spent half their day copying data from unstructured emails into their core policy systems and checking basic exclusions, leading to backlogs and delay in dispatching adjusters.
goals: Enable initial checks on policy coverage boundaries automatically.
Decrease First Notice of Loss (FNOL) triage time to minutes.
challenges: Unstructured Inputs: Emails contained spelling errors, slang, and unstructured damage reports.
AI Hallucinations: AI agent could hallucinate policy clauses and draft misleading settlement offers.
requirements: Req 01: Extract claimant name, policy number, date of loss, and description from emails.
Req 02: Query policy DB via API to confirm active coverage on the date of loss.
Req 03: Draft standard claim summaries and request missing details from policyholders automatically.
insureai.solution: An AI automation pipeline (via Make.com and OpenAI APIs). When an email is received, the LLM parses the text into a JSON object, checks the database for policy status, matches damage category to policy inclusions, and populates the claims database for staff approval.
insureai.workflows: Incoming claim email → Make.com trigger → OpenAI parse and structure text → Policy verification API lookup → Policy active checks → Draft confirmation and log to CRM database.
insureai.wireframes: Designed a dashboard review view where operators see the side-by-side view of the original email, parsed AI fields, policy check results, and a draft email for review.
userStories: As a Claims Manager, I want to review the parsed AI fields and approve them before writing to the database so that errors are caught.
As an Auditor, I want the system to link the exact prompt version used to generate the claim analysis for compliance records.
insureai.acceptanceCriteria: Given an incoming claim email has been processed, when the policy check API returns 'EXPIRED' status, then the system must flag the claim as 'Needs Review - Coverage Issue' and draft an email requesting premium logs.
insureai.apiRequirements: POST /api/v1/claims/triage\\nPayload: { 'raw_email_text': 'My kitchen flooded last night on 2026-07-16. Policy ID is P-0091...' }\\nResponse: { 'policy_id': 'P-0091', 'date_of_loss': '2026-07-16', 'extracted_damage': 'Water damage in kitchen', 'status': 'VALIDATED' }
insureai.uat: Tested 100 historical claims through the pipeline to audit accuracy against professional adjuster judgments.
insureai.outcome: Claims processing speed improved by 99%, reducing initial triage delay from 3 days to under 10 minutes. The LLM extraction accuracy achieved 94%.
insureai.lessons: Having human-in-the-loop review was critical for edge cases. Rather than automating approvals entirely, we structured it to support the staff, which eased deployment stress.

talentstream.background: TalentStream was developed for an executive recruitment agency managing high-volume tech hiring across multiple client accounts. Recruiters handled 500+ candidate CVs weekly in diverse formats.
talentstream.problem: Recruiters spent 70% of their day manually reading CVs and checking skill keywords, leading to missed top-tier candidates and high time-to-hire delays.
goals: Automate semantic resume parsing and skill matching.
Integrate automated calendar scheduling for interview stages.
challenges: Varied CV Formats: Parsing non-standard multi-column PDF and Word document resume layouts.
Keyword Bias: Ensuring candidate scoring ranks relevant experience rather than exact keyword matches.
requirements: Req 01: Parse PDF/DOCX resumes into structured candidate profiles automatically.
Req 02: Score candidate profiles against job description criteria with match percentages.
Req 03: Trigger automated interview invitation links upon recruiter approval.
talentstream.solution: A custom Applicant Tracking System (ATS) combining AI resume parsing with interactive Kanban pipeline boards and automated candidate scheduling workflows.
talentstream.workflows: Candidate submits CV → AI parses work history & skills → Match engine scores CV against Job Requirements → Recruiter reviews top ranked candidates → 1-click invitation sends scheduling link to applicant.
talentstream.wireframes: Created Figma mockups detailing candidate pipeline kanban, resume viewer split-screen, and match score analytics.
userStories: As a Recruiter, I want to see a match score breakdown for each candidate so that I can prioritize reviewing top-fit applicants.
As a Hiring Manager, I want to view candidate summaries on mobile so that I can approve interview stages on the go.
talentstream.acceptanceCriteria: Given a candidate submits a PDF resume, when the parser processes the document, then all work experience dates, skill tags, and contact details must populate the candidate CRM profile within 5 seconds.
talentstream.uat: Conducted UAT with 8 talent recruiters across 50 real candidate submissions, refining match scoring logic based on recruiter feedback.
talentstream.outcome: Screening time dropped by 60%, and interview turnout rose by 25% due to automated SMS/Slack reminder nudges.
talentstream.lessons: Providing recruiters with a split-screen view showing original PDF next to AI extracted fields built immediate trust in automated parsing.

learnflow.background: LearnFlow was created for a multi-regional corporate client needing to deliver mandatory compliance, cybersecurity, and ethics training to 3,000+ employees.
learnflow.problem: Legacy training software suffered from 35% non-compliance rates because employees found the UI clunky and managers lacked visibility into upcoming deadlines.
goals: Achieve 95%+ compliance training completion across all departments.
Automate deadline reminder workflows via Slack and Email.
Deliver bite-sized, mobile-friendly interactive learning modules.
challenges: Employee Engagement: Overcoming training fatigue with interactive, gamified micro-learning units.
Multi-Regional Compliance: Managing different deadline requirements across geographic branches.
requirements: Req 01: Track real-time progress for mandatory compliance modules per employee and department.
Req 02: Automatically issue verified completion certificates upon quiz passing (>=80%).
Req 03: Trigger automated manager escalation alerts for overdue employee modules.
learnflow.solution: A responsive LMS platform featuring bite-sized course cards, real-time compliance progress bars, automated Slack/email reminders, and manager reporting dashboards.
learnflow.workflows: HR assigns compliance module → Employee receives Slack nudge → Employee completes 10-min module & quiz → System issues digital certificate & updates HR compliance ledger.
learnflow.wireframes: Mocked course catalog grid, video player with interactive quiz popups, and department compliance reporting tables.
userStories: As an Employee, I want to resume my course from where I left off on my mobile phone so that I can learn on the go.
As a Compliance Officer, I want to export real-time completion audit logs so that I can verify regulatory compliance.
learnflow.acceptanceCriteria: Given an employee completes a mandatory compliance module with a score >= 80%, when they submit the final quiz, then the system must mark the requirement 'Completed', issue a PDF certificate, and log the audit timestamp.
learnflow.uat: Executed UAT with 50 pilot users across HR, IT, and Finance departments. Achieved 100% completion in pilot run.
learnflow.outcome: Enterprise compliance completion jumped from 65% to 98.4% within 30 days of launch, while support tickets dropped by 40%.
learnflow.lessons: Bite-sized 10-minute training modules combined with automated Slack nudges drastically outperformed long 2-hour video sessions.
